source_text: Magistrum vero Gentium rationem privilegio auctoritatis armantem pronuntiasse, quia per unum hominem in hunc mundum culpa transierit, quo nomine separavit opera nuptiarum, quae sine duorum negotio esse non possunt, commendavimusque ob hoc ab illo unum fuisse nominatum, ne quis duos intellegere auderet.
pass_a_gloss: But that the Teacher of the Gentiles, arming reason with the privilege of authority, pronounced that through one human being guilt passed into this world, by which name he separated the works of marriages, which cannot be without the business of two, and we have commended that for this one was named by him, lest anyone dare to understand two.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: The Teacher of the Gentiles armed reason with the special force of authority by declaring that guilt passed into this world through one man (Romans 5:12). By this expression he excluded the activities of marriage, which cannot occur without the participation of two. We emphasized that he named one precisely so that no one would dare understand two.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian's pair with iustitia: guilt as culpable will, not a nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
